# FIPS 140-3 Support Analysis for Keycloak Runtime Logs

Generated: 2026-06-11

## Scope

This report compares the Keycloak FIPS runtime evidence in `.ai/reports` with the local NIST/CSRC reference corpus in `.ai/fips/references`. It classifies observed Keycloak encryption algorithms, BCJSSE TLS protocols and cipher suites, and all instantiable JCA/JCE service algorithm names from the runtime probe.

Important distinction: an algorithm can be NIST-approved in principle while the runtime observation is still not acceptable as FIPS evidence if the algorithm is instantiable from a provider that is outside the validated/approved provider boundary, or if key sizes, curves, modes, IV/nonce rules, service indicators, or approved-mode restrictions are not proven.

## Executive Result

The current Keycloak page and runtime evidence are not sufficient for a FIPS 140-3 support claim. FIPS 140-3 needs the SP 800-140C/D current allowlists, service-level approved security service indicators, SP 800-140B-style service/security policy mapping, and stricter handling of non-approved algorithms in approved mode. The same runtime provider exposure gaps found for FIPS 140-2 also apply here.
